author: Joey Cooke
title: 2025 season underway as practices begin - NewsBreak
text: MONROE COUNTY — The 2025 high school sports season got underway July 28 as 27 teams local stepped onto the course, field, court and pool on the campuses of Key West, Marathon, Coral Shores and Basilica. As it was for last fall, the Key West Conchs will have Johnny Hughes back on the sidelines for his 17th year as coach of the football team; Kim Butler will once again lead the volleyball squad; Keara McGraw will coach the boys and girls cross country squads; Josh Bassett will lead the golf program; and for a 27th season, Lori Bosco will lead the swimmers. The lone change for the Conchs in the fall is Madison Garcia as the new cheerleading coach. In Marathon, Sean McDonald returns as football coach, Kelly Cruz remains volleyball coach and Mary Coleman still leads the golf program. The major change will be Jim Murphy stepping away from the cross country, a program he led to a decade-long run to the state championships. Taking control of the state powerhouse team will be Helena Bursa and Shannon Wiley. Coral Shores is returning its coaching staff. Sam Ovale, who stepped aside during the 2024 campaign, is back as the coach of the Lady Canes volleyball squad. Ed Holly continues as coach of the football team. Jon Olsen heads the swim team coach. Gabe Suarez leads the cross country team and Danielle Thomas will further the growth of the golf program. Adding two varsity programs this fall will be Basilica: cross country, which will be coached by JJ Noah, and golf, mentored by Justin Smoot. Principal Robert Wright is expected to be on the court again for the volleyball program. With preseason officially underway, the teams have another few weeks to prepare for what 2025 has in store.
